Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Doubling the rate corresponds to only ~10°C rise for typical reactions. B: Quadrupling corresponds to ~20°C rise. D: Temperature definitely affects reaction rate.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Le Chatelier's principle states that when a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it
Option A: will always shift to the right to produce more products
Option B: shifts in the direction that opposes the applied change to re-establish equilibrium
Option C: will stop reacting until the disturbance is removed
Option D: shifts in the direction that increases the disturbance
Explanation: Le Chatelier's principle: if a stress (change in concentration, pressure, or temperature) is applied to a system at equilibrium, the equilibrium position shifts in the direction that tends to counteract or relieve that stress.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: The direction of shift depends on the nature of the stress, not always to the right. C: The system does not stop; it shifts to a new equilibrium. D: The system opposes (not increases) the disturbance.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: In the reaction N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g), increasing pressure at constant temperature will
Option A: shift equilibrium to the right (more NO2)
Option B: shift equilibrium to the left (more N2O4)
Option C: have no effect on the equilibrium
Explanation: Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas. Left side: 1 mol gas; Right side: 2 mol gas. Increased pressure shifts equilibrium to the LEFT (fewer moles of gas = N2O4 side).
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Shifting right would produce MORE gas (2 mol), which opposes increased pressure — incorrect. C: Pressure change affects equilibria involving gases with unequal moles. D: Kc is only affected by temperature, not pressure.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The equilibrium constant K for a reaction is only affected by changes in
Explanation: The equilibrium constant K is a thermodynamic quantity that depends only on temperature. Changing concentration or pressure shifts the equilibrium position but K remains the same. A catalyst only speeds up reaching equilibrium without changing K.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Concentration changes shift position but K is unchanged. B: Pressure changes shift position but K is unchanged. C: Catalyst speeds up reaching equilibrium but does not change K.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: In the Haber process for ammonia synthesis: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3 (ΔH = -92kJ/mol). To maximize NH3 yield, one should use
Explanation: Forward reaction: 4 mol gas → 2 mol gas (decrease), so high pressure favours NH3. Forward reaction is exothermic, so lower temperature favours NH3. However, lower temperature slows rate — industry uses ~450°C as a compromise.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: High temperature shifts equilibrium to left (less NH3); low pressure also gives less NH3. C: High temperature shifts equilibrium left (endothermic direction). D: Low pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with more gas (left = less NH3).

Subject: Chemistry
Question: A reaction at equilibrium can be described as
Option A: A reaction that has stopped completely
Option B: A state where the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
Option C: A reaction with no reactants remaining
Option D: A state where concentrations are all equal
Explanation: Dynamic equilibrium: both forward and reverse reactions continue, but at equal rates. Concentrations remain constant (not necessarily equal) because formation rate equals consumption rate for each species.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: At equilibrium both reactions continue (dynamic). C: Some reactants always remain at equilibrium (reversible reaction). D: Concentrations are constant, not necessarily equal.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: When steam reacts with iron: 3Fe + 4H2O ⇌ Fe3O4 + 4H2, removing H2 from the equilibrium mixture will
Option C: shift equilibrium to the right, producing more Fe3O4
Explanation: Removing a product (H2) reduces its concentration on the right side. By Le Chatelier's principle, the equilibrium shifts to the RIGHT to replace the removed H2, producing more Fe3O4 and consuming more Fe and H2O.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Removing product shifts equilibrium to the right, not left. B: The shift to the right maintains or increases rate of forward reaction. D: Changing concentration of a component definitely affects equilibrium.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Chlorine is prepared in the laboratory by
Option A: Burning chlorine gas in excess oxygen
Option B: Oxidation of concentrated HCl with MnO2 and heat
Option D: Reaction of NaCl with dilute H2SO4
Explanation: Laboratory preparation of Cl2: MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + Cl2 + 2H2O. MnO2 oxidizes the HCl. The Cl2 produced is dried and collected by upward displacement of air (denser than air).
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Cl2 is not produced by burning; it is a product of oxidation of HCl. C: Electrolysis of water produces H2 and O2. D: Dilute H2SO4 with NaCl only produces NaHSO4 and HCl gas; concentrated H2SO4 produces HCl (not Cl2).

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The industrial preparation of chlorine is by
Option A: Deacon's process (oxidation of HCl with air)
Explanation: Industrially, chlorine is manufactured by the electrolysis of brine: Chlorine is produced at the anode, hydrogen at the cathode, and NaOH in solution. This is the chlor-alkali process.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Deacon's process is historical; the modern method is electrolysis. C: The Haber process produces ammonia (NH3). D: The Contact process produces sulphuric acid.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The test for a chloride (Cl-) ion in solution involves
Option A: Adding BaCl2 solution in dilute HCl
Option B: Adding dilute HNO3 then AgNO3 solution; a white precipitate insoluble in excess HNO3 but soluble in NH3
Explanation: Test for Cl-: Add dilute HNO3 (to remove carbonate/sulphite interference), then add AgNO3 solution. Cl- + Ag+ → AgCl↓ (white precipitate). AgCl is insoluble in dilute HNO3 but dissolves in dilute NH3 solution.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: BaCl2 tests for SO4 2-, not Cl-. C: Litmus tests for acidity/alkalinity. D: NaOH tests for metal cations.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The bleaching action of chlorine is due to
Option B: Formation of nascent oxygen from HOCl (hypochlorous acid) which oxidizes the dye
Option D: Reduction of the dye by Cl2
Explanation: Cl2 + H2O → HCl + HOCl. HOCl → HCl + [O] (nascent oxygen). The nascent oxygen is a powerful oxidizing agent that destroys (oxidizes) the coloured organic compounds (dyes), causing bleaching.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Cl2 alone cannot bleach — it must be moist (react with water). C: Acidity does not cause bleaching. D: Bleaching is an oxidation process, not reduction.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Ozone (O3) is important in the atmosphere because it
Option C: absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun, protecting life on Earth
Option D: helps in the formation of acid rain
Explanation: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs UV-B and UV-C radiation from the sun. Without this protection, increased UV radiation would cause skin cancer, cataracts, and damage to ecosystems.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: O2 (oxygen), not O3, is used for breathing. B: Ozone absorbs UV, not reflects sunlight. D: Ozone is beneficial; it is ozone depletion that is harmful; CFCs/NOx cause acid rain.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The industrial preparation of H2SO4 by the Contact Process involves which key oxidation step?
Explanation: The key (and rate-determining) step in the Contact Process is the catalytic oxidation of SO2 to SO3: 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3, using a vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) catalyst at 450°C and 1-2 atm. SO3 is then absorbed into oleum.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Burning S to SO2 is only the first step. C: Direct absorption of SO3 in water is explosive; it is absorbed in concentrated H2SO4 to form oleum. D: H2S is not a reactant in the Contact Process.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Ammonia (NH3) is prepared industrially by the
Option A: Contact process from N2 and H2
Option B: Haber process from N2 and H2
Option C: Solvay process from NaCl and NH3
Explanation: The Haber process: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3. Conditions: iron catalyst, ~450°C, ~200 atm pressure. This is the standard industrial production of ammonia.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: The Contact process makes H2SO4, not NH3. C: The Solvay process makes Na2CO3 (sodium carbonate). D: Liquid nitrogen is N2 and does not yield NH3 by electrolysis.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The test for NH4+ (ammonium ion) involves
Option C: Adding NaOH solution and warming — ammonia gas (turns moist red litmus blue) is produced
Explanation: Test for NH4+: Add NaOH solution and warm gently. NH4+ + OH- → NH3↑ + H2O. The ammonia gas produced turns moist red litmus paper blue and has a characteristic pungent smell.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: AgNO3 tests for halide ions. B: BaCl2 tests for SO4 2-. D: Effervescence with HCl occurs with carbonates (CO3 2-).

Subject: Chemistry
Question: When HNO3 reacts with copper, which gas is produced?
Explanation: Copper does not displace H2 from acid (it is below H in the reactivity series). HNO3 oxidizes Cu: Concentrated HNO3 → NO2 (brown gas); Dilute HNO3 → NO (colourless gas that turns brown in air). Cu → Cu2+.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Cu is below H2 in the reactivity series and does not produce H2 with acids. B: O2 is not produced from this reaction. D: SO2 would be from reaction with H2SO4, not HNO3.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Carbon (II) oxide (CO) is dangerous to humans because
Option B: It forms carboxyhaemoglobin, preventing oxygen transport in blood
Option C: It reacts with water in the lungs
Option D: It has a strong unpleasant smell
Explanation: CO binds to haemoglobin with 200-300 times greater affinity than O2, forming carboxyhaemoglobin (COHb). This prevents O2 from being transported in the blood, causing oxygen deprivation and death. CO is odourless.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: CO is not acidic; CO2 is weakly acidic. C: CO does not react significantly with water in the lungs. D: CO is odourless and colourless — this is part of what makes it dangerous.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Which of the following is an allotrope of carbon?
Explanation: Allotropes are different physical forms of the same element. Carbon's allotropes include diamond, graphite, and fullerenes (buckminsterfullerene). Dry ice (CO2), CO2, and CO are compounds of carbon, not allotropes.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Dry ice is solid CO2 — a compound. C: CO2 is a compound (two elements). D: CO is a compound (two elements).

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Hydrogen sulphide (H2S) acts as a precipitating agent in qualitative analysis because
Option B: S2- ions precipitate many insoluble metal sulphides with distinctive colours
Option D: it acts as an oxidizing agent
Explanation: H2S ionizes to provide S2- ions. Many metal sulphides are insoluble and have characteristic colours: CuS (black), ZnS (white), PbS (black), FeS (black). This allows identification of metal ions in qualitative analysis.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: H2S is a WEAK acid (weak electrolyte). C: Many metal sulphides are insoluble. D: H2S is a REDUCING agent (it loses electrons/hydrogen), not an oxidizing agent.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The test for CO3 2- (carbonate ion) involves
Option A: Adding AgNO3 — white precipitate soluble in NH3
Option B: Adding dilute HCl — brisk effervescence of CO2 which turns Ca(OH)2 solution milky
Option C: Adding BaCl2 in HCl — white precipitate
Explanation: Test for CO3 2-: Add dilute HCl. CO3 2- + 2H+ → H2O + CO2↑. The CO2 gas produced turns limewater (Ca(OH)2 solution) milky: Ca(OH)2 + CO2 → CaCO3↓ + H2O.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: AgNO3 tests for Cl- (and other halides). C: BaCl2 in HCl tests for SO4 2-. D: NaOH tests for NH4+ (when warmed) or metal cations.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The nitrogen cycle is important because it
Option A: removes all nitrogen from the atmosphere permanently
Option B: circulates nitrogen between the atmosphere, soil, living organisms, and back to the atmosphere
Option C: produces nitrogen from oxygen in the air
Option D: converts all nitrogen to nitric acid
Explanation: The nitrogen cycle is the biogeochemical cycle by which nitrogen is converted between N2 in the atmosphere, nitrates in soil (via fixation and nitrification), amino acids in organisms, and back to N2 (via denitrification). It maintains nitrogen availability for life.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: N2 levels remain relatively constant — the cycle recycles N. C: Nitrogen is fixed FROM the atmosphere (N2→NH3/NO3-), not produced from O2. D: Only a fraction becomes nitric acid.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Sulphur exists as rhombic and monoclinic allotropes. These differ in
Option C: crystal structure and stability at different temperatures
Explanation: Rhombic sulphur (stable below 96°C) and monoclinic sulphur (stable above 96°C, below melting point) are allotropes of S8 with different crystal structures (packing arrangements). They have the same chemical properties but different physical properties.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Both allotropes have the same formula (S8 molecules). B: Both are pure sulphur atoms. D: While they may appear slightly different, the distinction is fundamentally about crystal structure and temperature stability.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Products obtained from the destructive distillation of coal include
Option B: Coal gas, coal tar, ammoniacal liquor, and coke
Explanation: Destructive distillation of coal (heating without air) produces: coal gas (fuel), coal tar (source of aromatic compounds), ammoniacal liquor (contains NH3), and coke (nearly pure carbon used as fuel and in metallurgy).
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: These are products of petroleum, not coal. C: These simple alkanes are in natural gas/coal gas but the complete list is broader. D: Graphite and diamond are not products of destructive distillation.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The Solvay process is used for the industrial production of
Explanation: The Solvay (ammonia-soda) process manufactures Na2CO3 (washing soda) using NaCl, NH3, CO2, and water as raw materials. The overall reaction: 2NaCl + CaCO3 → Na2CO3 + CaCl2.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: NaOH is produced by electrolysis of brine. C: NaCl occurs naturally in sea water and mines. D: NH3 is made by the Haber process.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The reaction of sodium hydroxide with aluminium metal produces
Option B: NaAlO2 + H2↑ (sodium aluminate and hydrogen gas)
Explanation: Aluminium is amphoteric. It reacts with both acids and alkalis: 2Al + 2NaOH + 2H2O → 2NaAlO2 + 3H2↑. NaOH dissolves Al, producing sodium aluminate and hydrogen gas.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: No NaCl is produced; there is no Cl present. C: Al(OH)3 forms when Al3+ reacts with dilute NaOH (insufficient excess). D: Al does react with NaOH (it is amphoteric).

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Which property distinguishes transition metals from typical s-block metals?
Option B: They have variable oxidation states and form coloured compounds
Option C: They all have the same electron configuration
Option D: They are all harder than iron
Explanation: Transition metals have incompletely filled d-orbitals (in the atom or common ions), which give rise to: variable oxidation states (different d-electron loss), coloured compounds (d-d electron transitions absorb visible light), and catalytic activity.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Only Fe, Co, Ni are ferromagnetic. C: Transition metals have different configurations. D: Hardness varies among transition metals.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Iron is extracted from its oxide ores in a blast furnace using
Option A: Carbon monoxide as the reducing agent
Option D: Coke directly reacting without any intermediate
Explanation: In the blast furnace, coke burns to form CO2, which reacts with more coke to form CO (C + CO2 → 2CO). CO is the main reducing agent: Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2. Some direct reduction by C also occurs.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: B: H2 is used for iron production in some modern DRI processes but CO is the standard blast furnace answer. C: Electrolysis is too expensive for large-scale iron production; it is used for Al. D: Coke does directly reduce at very high temperatures, but CO is the primary reducing agent.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Steel differs from cast iron in that steel has
Option A: Higher carbon content (3-4%) and is more brittle
Option B: Lower carbon content (0.1-1.5%) and is stronger and less brittle
Option D: More iron and less carbon than wrought iron
Explanation: Cast iron has ~3-4% carbon (brittle, hard). Steel has 0.1-1.5% carbon. Lowering carbon content makes the metal less brittle, more malleable, and tougher. Stainless steel also contains Cr and Ni for corrosion resistance.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: This describes cast iron, not steel. C: Pure iron contains no carbon; steel always has some carbon (0.1-1.5%). D: This is partially true for mild steel vs wrought iron but B is the most accurate complete answer.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The test for Fe2+ (iron(II) ions) involves
Option B: Adding NaOH — dirty green precipitate that turns brown on standing (oxidation)
Explanation: Fe2+ + 2OH- → Fe(OH)2↓ (dirty green precipitate). On standing in air, Fe(OH)2 is oxidized to Fe(OH)3: 4Fe(OH)2 + O2 + 2H2O → 4Fe(OH)3 (rust-brown). This colour change is characteristic of Fe2+.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Brown precipitate with NaOH indicates Fe3+ not Fe2+. C: AgNO3 tests for halide ions. D: BaCl2 tests for SO4 2-.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) (CuSO4) is prepared from copper by
Option A: Direct reaction of Cu with dilute H2SO4
Option B: Reacting Cu with hot concentrated H2SO4, or dissolving CuO/Cu2O in dilute H2SO4
Explanation: Cu does not react with dilute H2SO4 (below H in activity series). CuSO4 is prepared by: (1) Cu + 2H2SO4(conc.) → CuSO4 + SO2 + 2H2O (hot concentrated H2SO4), or (2) CuO + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + H2O.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Cu does NOT react with dilute H2SO4. C: Electrolysis is used to purify Cu, not directly make CuSO4. D: Cu does not react with HCl to form CuSO4.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Calcium oxide (quicklime) is used in the manufacture of cement. Its reaction with water is
Explanation: CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 (calcium hydroxide / slaked lime). This reaction is highly exothermic (produces a lot of heat). Slaked lime is used to make mortar and to adjust soil pH.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: The reaction is strongly EXOthermic, not endothermic. C: CaO reacts vigorously with water. D: CaCO3 and CO2 are not products of this reaction (wrong reagents).

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The percentage composition of cement is approximately
Option C: CaO, SiO2, Al2O3, and Fe2O3 (mainly CaO·SiO2 compounds)
Explanation: Portland cement is composed mainly of calcium silicates (CaO·SiO2 compounds), with alumina (Al2O3) and iron oxide (Fe2O3). The raw materials are limestone (CaCO3) and clay. CaCO3 is calcined to CaO during manufacture.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: CaCO3 is the raw material, not the final product. B: Ca3(PO4)2 is not a major component of cement. D: NaCl and CaSO4 are not components of cement.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: An alloy of copper and zinc is called
Explanation: Brass is an alloy of copper (Cu) and zinc (Zn). It is harder than copper and has good corrosion resistance. Bronze is Cu + Sn (tin). Solder is Pb + Sn. Duralumin is Al + Cu + Mg + Mn.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Bronze = Cu + Sn. C: Solder = Pb + Sn (soft solder) or Ag + Cu (hard solder). D: Duralumin = Al alloy (with Cu, Mg, Mn).

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The purification of bauxite (aluminium ore) to obtain pure Al2O3 is called
Explanation: The Bayer process purifies bauxite by dissolving Al2O3 in hot concentrated NaOH (leaving Fe2O3 and SiO2 residue), then precipitating Al(OH)3, which is calcined to pure Al2O3. The Hall-Héroult process then electrolyzes this to obtain Al.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: The Hall-Héroult process is the electrolytic EXTRACTION of Al from purified Al2O3. C: Solvay process makes Na2CO3. D: Contact process makes H2SO4.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The test for Cu2+ ions involves
Explanation: Test for Cu2+: Add NaOH solution. Cu2+ + 2OH- → Cu(OH)2↓ (blue precipitate). Cu(OH)2 dissolves in excess concentrated NH3 to form a deep blue [Cu(NH3)4]2+ complex (further confirmation).
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: White precipitate with NaOH indicates Al3+, Zn2+, or Ca2+. C: AgNO3 is not used to test for Cu2+. D: BaCl2 tests for SO4 2-.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The general formula for alkanes is
Explanation: Alkanes (saturated hydrocarbons) have the general formula CnH2n+2 where n is the number of carbon atoms. Example: methane (n=1) = CH4 = CnH2n+2 ✓
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: CnH2n is the formula for alkenes (one double bond). B: CnH2n-2 is the formula for alkynes (triple bond) or cycloalkenes. D: CnH2n+1 is the formula for an alkyl GROUP, not a complete molecule.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Which of the following is an example of structural isomerism?
Explanation: Structural isomers have the same molecular formula (C4H10) but different structural arrangements. Butane (straight chain) and methylpropane (branched) both have formula C4H10 — they are structural isomers.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Cis and trans but-2-ene are GEOMETRIC (stereoisomers). C: 12C and 13C are isotopes, not isomers. D: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The IUPAC name of CH3CH2CH2OH is
Explanation: The compound has a 3-carbon chain (prop-), an OH group (-ol) on carbon 1 (-1-). The IUPAC name is propan-1-ol. The locant '1' specifies the position of the OH group on the chain.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: 'Propanol' is ambiguous (could be propan-1-ol or propan-2-ol); IUPAC requires the locant. C: '1-Propyl alcohol' is not an acceptable IUPAC format. D: Propanal (CH3CH2CHO) is the aldehyde, not the alcohol.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Which reagent is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols (Lucas test)?
Option C: Concentrated HCl and anhydrous ZnCl2 (Lucas reagent)
Explanation: Lucas test: Concentrated HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2. The alcohol reacts to form an alkyl chloride (turbidity/cloudiness). Rate: 3° alcohol reacts immediately, 2° within 5 min (warming), 1° alcohol does not react (or very slowly with heat).
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: K2Cr2O7/H2SO4 distinguishes oxidizable alcohols (1°→aldehyde/acid, 2°→ketone) from 3° (no reaction) by colour change. B: Fehling's distinguishes aldehydes from ketones. D: Tollens' distinguishes aldehydes from ketones.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Ethanol can be produced industrially by fermentation of
Option C: Direct hydration of ethylene over acid catalyst
Option D: Both B and C are industrial methods
Explanation: Industrial production of ethanol uses TWO methods: (1) Fermentation: C6H12O6 → 2C2H5OH + 2CO2 (using yeast/zymase), and (2) Catalytic hydration: C2H4 + H2O → C2H5OH (H3PO4 catalyst, 300°C). The JAMB syllabus mentions both.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Ethyne + H2 gives ethylene (hydrogenation), not ethanol directly. B: Fermentation is one industrial method but the question asks for all industrial methods. C: Hydration is one industrial method but not the only one.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The functional group of alkanals (aldehydes) is
Explanation: The aldehyde functional group is -CHO (formyl group), where the carbonyl carbon (C=O) has at least one hydrogen atom attached. For example, ethanal (CH3CHO) has this group at the end of the chain.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: -OH is the alcohol (alkanol) functional group. B: -COOH is the carboxylic acid (alkanoic acid) functional group. D: -CO- (internal carbonyl) is the ketone (alkanone) functional group.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol to form
Explanation: Esterification: CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O. Ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate (ester) + water. H2SO4 is the catalyst.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Ethane would require reduction, not esterification. C: Diethyl ether is formed from two molecules of alcohol, not acid + alcohol. D: Ethyne formation requires different conditions.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Which of the following tests would give a POSITIVE result with ethanal (CH3CHO) but NOT with propanone (CH3COCH3)?
Explanation: Fehling's solution (alkaline Cu2+) oxidizes ALDEHYDES to carboxylic acids, producing a brick-red (Cu2O) precipitate. KETONES are NOT oxidized by Fehling's. Tollens' silver mirror test also distinguishes them.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Na2CO3 effervescence tests for carboxylic acids; neither CHO nor ketones react. C: Bromine water tests for unsaturation (alkenes) or phenol, not this distinction. D: 2,4-DNP reacts with BOTH aldehydes and ketones (both have C=O).

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Saponification is the process of
Option B: Hydrolysis of fats/oils (alkanoates) with NaOH or KOH to produce soap and glycerol
Option C: Fermentation of sugars to produce alcohol
Explanation: Saponification: fat/oil (ester of glycerol + long-chain fatty acids) + NaOH → sodium soap (sodium salt of fatty acid) + glycerol. The JAMB syllabus specifically mentions saponification as alkanoate hydrolysis.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Synthetic rubber production uses polymerization of isoprene/butadiene. C: Fermentation produces alcohol from sugars. D: Cracking breaks long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter ones.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The octane number of petrol is a measure of
Option A: The number of carbon atoms in petrol
Option B: The percentage of octane in the mixture
Option C: The anti-knock quality of petrol (resistance to premature ignition)
Explanation: The octane number (octane rating) is a measure of a fuel's ability to resist knocking (premature detonation) in an engine. Higher octane = better anti-knock performance. 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (isooctane) is assigned octane number 100.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Petrol contains many hydrocarbons; the octane number is not about counting carbons. B: It is a rating scale from 0-100, not a percentage. D: Density is a physical property measured separately.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Polythene (polyethene) is produced by
Explanation: Polythene is an addition polymer formed when many ethene monomers (CH2=CH2) join together by breaking their double bonds: nCH2=CH2 → (-CH2-CH2-)n. No small molecule is lost in addition polymerization.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Condensation polymerization produces polyesters, nylon, etc. with loss of H2O. C: Fermentation produces ethanol, not polythene. D: Cracking of propene yields smaller hydrocarbons, not polythene.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Proteins are polymers of
Option A: Amino acids joined by peptide bonds
Option B: Glucose units joined by glycosidic bonds
Option C: Fatty acids joined by ester bonds
Explanation: Proteins are polypeptides — chains of amino acid monomers joined by peptide bonds (-CO-NH-) formed by condensation reactions between the amino (-NH2) and carboxyl (-COOH) groups of adjacent amino acids.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: B: Glucose units joined by glycosidic bonds describes polysaccharides (starch, cellulose). C: Fatty acids + glycerol joined by ester bonds describes fats/oils. D: Nucleotides in phosphodiester bonds describes DNA/RNA.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The Biuret test is used to detect
Explanation: The Biuret test detects proteins: add NaOH, then dilute CuSO4. If protein (peptide bonds) is present, the solution turns purple/violet. The Cu2+ coordinates with peptide bonds. The JAMB syllabus lists Biuret as one of the protein tests.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Glucose is tested with Fehling's/Benedict's (brick-red precipitate). B: Starch is tested with iodine solution (blue-black colour). D: Lipids are tested with ethanol-water emulsion test.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Cellulose is obtained from cotton. In terms of carbohydrate classification, cellulose is
Explanation: Cellulose is a polysaccharide — a polymer of β-glucose units linked by β-1,4-glycosidic bonds. It forms the structural component of plant cell walls. Monosaccharides = single units (glucose). Disaccharides = 2 units (sucrose). Polysaccharides = many units.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Monosaccharides: glucose, fructose, galactose (single sugar units). B: Disaccharides: sucrose, maltose, lactose (2 sugar units). D: 'Trisaccharide' is not one of the standard JAMB classification categories.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Benzene (C6H6) is an aromatic compound that is more stable than expected because of
Option A: Its ring structure with alternating single and double bonds
Option B: Delocalization of π electrons over all six carbon atoms (resonance stabilization)
Option C: The presence of six hydrogen atoms
Explanation: Benzene's exceptional stability (resistance to addition reactions) arises from the delocalization of the six π electrons uniformly over the ring (resonance hybrid). This makes it 150 kJ/mol more stable than a hypothetical cyclohexatriene.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: This describes a Kekulé structure; the real benzene has equal C-C bonds due to delocalization. C: The H atoms are standard; stability comes from electron delocalization. D: High boiling point is a consequence, not the cause of stability.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Natural rubber is a polymer of
Explanation: Natural rubber (polyisoprene) is a polymer of isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene, CH2=C(CH3)-CH=CH2). The double bonds polymerize to form the long-chain polymer. The JAMB syllabus explicitly mentions this.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Polyethene (polythene) is the polymer of ethene. B: Polypropylene is the polymer of propene. D: Polystyrene is the polymer of styrene.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The process of vulcanization of rubber involves
Option B: Cross-linking rubber chains with sulphur to improve strength and elasticity
Option C: Adding carbon black to improve colour
Explanation: Vulcanization (discovered by Goodyear) involves heating natural rubber with sulphur. Sulphur atoms form cross-links (bridges) between adjacent polymer chains, making the rubber stronger, more elastic, less tacky, and more resistant to heat and chemicals.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Antioxidants preserve rubber but are not vulcanization. C: Carbon black reinforces rubber but is not vulcanization. D: Dissolving in benzene gives rubber solution (used as adhesive) but is not vulcanization.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: What is the structural feature that distinguishes a primary alcohol from a secondary alcohol?
Option A: A primary alcohol has more carbon atoms
Option B: In a primary alcohol, the carbon bearing the OH group is attached to only one other carbon atom
Option C: A secondary alcohol has a higher boiling point
Option D: A primary alcohol is more reactive
Explanation: Classification: Primary alcohol: -OH on C attached to 1 C (e.g., CH3CH2OH). Secondary alcohol: -OH on C attached to 2 C atoms (e.g., (CH3)2CHOH). Tertiary: -OH on C attached to 3 C atoms.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Number of carbons doesn't determine primary/secondary classification. C: Boiling point is a property, not the structural definition. D: Reactivity toward oxidation differs (1° and 2° can be oxidized; 3° cannot) but this is a consequence, not the definition.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Nylon is an example of
Explanation: Nylon is a synthetic polyamide — a condensation polymer formed by the reaction of a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine, with loss of water (H2O) for each amide bond (-CO-NH-) formed. It is a thermoplastic.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Addition polymers (polythene, PVC) form with no small molecule loss. C: Natural polymers include cellulose, silk, natural rubber. D: Nylon is a thermoplastic (can be remoulded); thermosetting plastics (bakelite) cannot.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The cracking of petroleum fractions converts
Option A: Short chain alkanes into longer chain hydrocarbons
Option B: Long chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful ones (including alkenes)
Option C: Alkenes into alkanes by addition of H2
Option D: Crude oil into petrol by distillation
Explanation: Cracking breaks long-chain hydrocarbon molecules (from heavy fractions) into shorter, more useful molecules, including alkenes. Two types: thermal cracking (high temp/pressure) and catalytic cracking (zeolite catalyst at ~500°C).
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Cracking converts LONG chains to SHORT chains, not the reverse. C: This describes hydrogenation (reduction) of alkenes. D: Distillation separates fractions; cracking converts them.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Ethyne (acetylene) can be produced from
Option B: Action of water on calcium carbide (CaC2)
Explanation: CaC2 + 2H2O → Ca(OH)2 + C2H2↑. Calcium carbide reacts with water to produce ethyne (acetylene) gas. The JAMB syllabus explicitly cites this as the method of production of ethyne.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Fermentation produces ethanol. C: Dehydration of ethanol gives ethene (C2H4), not ethyne. D: Cracking methane primarily gives C and H2.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Fats and oils differ primarily in that at room temperature
Option A: Fats are liquid, oils are solid
Option B: Fats are solid (saturated), oils are liquid (unsaturated)
Option C: Fats contain phosphorus, oils do not
Option D: Fats are proteins, oils are lipids
Explanation: Fats (solid at room temp) are esters of glycerol and SATURATED fatty acids — packed tightly, high melting point. Oils (liquid at room temp) are esters of glycerol and UNSATURATED fatty acids — kinked chains, lower melting point.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: This is reversed. C: Phosphorus is in phospholipids, not in fats or oils. D: Both fats and oils are lipids (alkanoates); proteins are a completely different class.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The Ninhydrin test is used to detect the presence of
Explanation: Ninhydrin reacts with free amino groups (-NH2) of amino acids and proteins, producing a purple (Ruhemann's purple) colour. The JAMB syllabus lists Ninhydrin as one of the protein/amino acid tests.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Glucose is detected by Fehling's/Benedict's test. B: Starch is detected by iodine solution (blue-black). D: Lipids are detected by the emulsion test.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Thermoplastics differ from thermosetting plastics in that thermoplastics
Option B: Can be repeatedly softened by heating and remoulded (reversible)
Option D: Are made only from natural materials
Explanation: Thermoplastics (e.g., polythene, PVC, nylon) soften on heating and can be remoulded — their polymer chains are not cross-linked. Thermosetting plastics (e.g., Bakelite, melamine) have extensive cross-links and cannot be remoulded once set.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Thermoplastics CAN be recycled (this is their advantage). C: Thermosetting plastics are generally harder. D: Both types can be synthetic.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Biotechnology in the chemical industry involves
Option A: Using machines to speed up chemical production
Option B: Using biological organisms or their products (enzymes, fermentation) in industrial processes
Option C: Adding biological compounds as fuel additives
Explanation: Biotechnology uses biological systems (bacteria, fungi, enzymes) for industrial purposes: fermentation (ethanol, antibiotics), enzyme-catalyzed reactions (food processing), bioremediation, and production of pharmaceuticals.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Using machines is automation/engineering. C: Fuel additives is a chemical engineering topic. D: Testing on animals is pharmaceutical safety testing, not biotechnology in industrial chemistry.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Fine chemicals differ from heavy chemicals in that fine chemicals
Option A: Are produced in large quantities for industrial use
Option B: Are produced in small quantities for specialized applications (pharmaceuticals, dyes, perfumes)
Option D: Are produced from biological sources only
Explanation: Fine chemicals: high purity, small quantities, high cost per gram, complex synthesis (pharmaceuticals, pesticides, dyes, perfumes, food additives). Heavy chemicals: large quantities, relatively cheap per unit (H2SO4, NaOH, Cl2, Na2CO3).
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: This describes heavy (bulk) chemicals. C: Fine chemicals are MORE expensive per gram due to purity and complexity. D: Fine chemicals can be synthetic or natural.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: Which of the following is a HEAVY chemical?
Explanation: Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) is the world's most produced heavy/bulk chemical, manufactured in millions of tonnes per year. It is used in fertilizer production, petroleum refining, and many industrial processes.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is a pharmaceutical = fine chemical. B: Penicillin is an antibiotic = fine chemical. D: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a pharmaceutical/food supplement = fine chemical.

Subject: Chemistry
Question: The primary raw material for the petrochemical industry is
Explanation: Petrochemicals are chemicals derived from petroleum (crude oil) and natural gas. These include plastics, synthetic fibres, detergents, solvents, and most organic chemicals produced industrially. They are the starting materials for organic synthesis.
Why Other Options Are Wrong: A: Coal is used in the coal-chemical industry (coke, coal tar) but is not the primary petrochemical feedstock. C: Sodium chloride is the raw material for the chlor-alkali industry. D: Limestone is for cement and Ca-based chemicals.
